t: Philip II turned Macedon from a raided frontier kingdom into the master of Greece with a pike phalanx and Companion cavalry.
Alexander the Great conquered the Achaemenid Empire from Egypt to the Indus, spreading Greek language and cities across Asia.
It split among his generals after 323 BCE, but their kingdoms created the Hellenistic world that Rome later absorbed.
dyk: Philip II's phalanx carried the sarissa, a pike of up to about six metres, letting several ranks present their points to the enemy at once.
ev: Philip II becomes king of Macedon and begins reforming its army
Philip defeats Athens and Thebes at Chaeronea and becomes master of Greece
Alexander crosses into Asia and wins his first victory at the Granicus
Alexander defeats Darius III at Gaugamela, sealing the fall of Persia
Alexander defeats Porus at the Hydaspes in India
Alexander dies at Babylon, leaving no clear successor
Rome defeats the last Antigonid king, Perseus, at Pydna
Macedonia becomes a Roman province, ending independent Macedonian rule
